name: The Dead and the Damned: Wraith Crossover Rules

pages.name: The Dead and the Damned: Wraith Crossover Rules

text.content:
Wraiths — the dead bound to unlife by passion and remorse — frequently become allies or pawns of centuries-old Kindred. Oblivion's Spectres rarely see into the Skinlands at all; Hierarchy wraiths are technically forbidden from contacting mortals; Kindred are most likely to run into wraiths of the illicit Guilds, Renegades, and Heretics. Since the Sixth Great Maelstrom, many such wraiths can only approach Kindred where a place in the living world corresponds to a safe haven in the Shadowlands (a cemetery over a Hierarchy Necropolis, an abandoned house serving as a Renegade Haunt).

The Shroud

Wraiths and the living are separated by the Shroud, a barrier of emotional distance and disbelief. It thins where mortal belief in ghosts is strong — graveyards, foggy roads, old attics, certain nights of the year — and thickens where it isn't: parking lots, shopping malls. Most Kindred havens and hangouts carry a moderate Shroud rating.

Guilds Most Likely to Interact with Kindred

Of the forbidden Guilds, four teach Arcanoi most likely to bring their wraiths into contact with vampires (independents using these Arcanoi are common too):

  • Embody: Lets a wraith manifest to a Kindred; a Cainite's long undead "life" makes an excellent long-term Embody attunement.
  • Outrage / Pandemonium: Spooks and Haunters use these to torment Kindred for Pathos. Kindred are especially vulnerable to frenzy triggered by Foul Humor's illusions of blood or windows opened in a haven with Death's Touch.
  • Puppetry: Attuning a Cainite gives a long-lasting Consort for possession.

How Wraiths Perceive Kindred

  • Deathsight: Lets a wraith spot a vampire hidden in a mortal crowd by her telltale signs of arrested death.
  • Lifesight: Functions like Aura Perception; most Kindred read with a distinctively pale aura.
  • Sharpened Senses: Lets a wraith pierce Cainite Chimerstry or Obfuscate as if the wraith had the basic levels of Auspex.

Spectres normally cannot use these to examine Kindred unless they possess the Arcanos Shroud Rending.

Disrupting an Incorporeal Wraith

A Cainite can disrupt a wraith simply by running through the space where the wraith is standing while it is incorporeal — this costs the wraith a Corpus Trait.

Haunts and the Spirit Mentor Merit

Wraiths commonly attach to vampires as haunts or as Spirit Mentors. A haunt with a Kindred as a Fetter, or one drawing Pathos from a vampire, is unlikely to destroy that Kindred outright (a wraith's Shadow is far less sentimental about it). A wraith aided by the Spirit Mentor Merit is more consistently helpful — usually possessing only basic Arcanoi, but providing a Cainite with extra eyes and ears in exchange for Pathos, other aid, or Fetter protection. Spirit Mentors are almost always wraiths, though a rogue Spectre with Shroud Rending manipulating a Cainite for its own cult is not unheard of. As a rule of thumb for Storyteller-character wraiths interacting with Kindred, keep them to no more than Intermediate Embody or Intermediate Pandemonium, and Basic level in other Arcanoi, unless running a high-powered game.

Necromancy-Using Clans

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls}, and the rare @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.33b61c8815714457]{Nagaraja} interact most with the Shadowlands. Solitary Heretic and Renegade wraiths tend to fear these Kindred for the power Necromancy grants them over the dead, while these Kindred in turn know better than to anger the Hierarchy or a powerful Circle.

Kindred Disciplines vs. Wraiths

  • Ash Path Necromancy: A vampire needs at least Shroudsight (its first level) to see past the Shroud. A wraith hiding via an Arcanos from a living observer tests against whichever is higher, the vampire's Auspex or Ash Path rating.
  • Auspex: A materialized or Embodied wraith can be read with Aura Perception; wraith auras don't halo but shimmer with color instead. Risen auras read identically to living vampires' auras. A Shadow is rumored (unverified) to appear as a muddy blot on a wraith's or Risen's aura.
  • Obfuscate: Any wraith may attempt to see through it using Lifesight plus a Mental Challenge.

Arcanoi vs. Kindred

  • Embody: An Embodied wraith is affected by any Discipline that works on ordinary mortals (Dominate, Presence), and Arcanoi normally hampered by the Shroud work on her without interference.
  • Fatalism: Doesn't always work across the Shroud on Kindred – spend an additional Mental Trait in the challenge. Fatal Vision, when it does work, lets the wraith witness the vampire's Embrace. At Storyteller discretion, an Embodied wraith may spend a Willpower Trait to perform Requiem, forcing a vampire into or out of frenzy.
  • Moliate: Works only on wraithly plasm, never on living flesh (Vicissitude is the reverse) — the two Disciplines/Arcanoi don't affect each other's target types.
  • Outrage: Death's Touch can ignite clothing but not undead flesh. Obliviate works normally on vampires and can be soaked with Fortitude.
  • Pandemonium: Blood created with this Arcanos is unusable to vampires and causes violent vomiting if consumed. A vampire targeted by Tempus Fugit cannot gain further extra actions from Celerity, though Tempus Fugit can negate Celerity's existing extra actions.
  • Phantasm: Affects vampires the same as mortals — they can be pulled into dreamscapes. While in a dreamscape, a Kindred may not spend blood or use Disciplines.
  • Puppetry: An aware Kindred may make a Willpower Challenge, or spend two Willpower Traits, to force the wraith out. If Dominate and Puppetry commands conflict, vampire and wraith resolve it with a Willpower Challenge; the loser cannot override the winner's commands until the following night.
  • Usury: Cannot be used to steal blood, or to steal/restore health levels between vampires.

Other Notes

  • Wraiths cannot be fed from, ghouled, or Embraced, even while Embodied. The rare Nagaraja Discipline Nihilistics (via Soul Feasting) is the sole exception, letting a vampire feast on a wraith directly.
  • Kindred who suffer Final Death occasionally return as wraiths, though rarely as Risen (Rising requires a reasonably intact body, and ancient vampire remains often crumble to dust). Kindred who achieve Golconda or who are diablerized never become wraiths.
  • A Risen (a wraith who reanimated her own body) can learn Celerity, Potence, Fortitude, and Obfuscate, making infiltration of Kindred society plausible — until someone tries to feed from her and gets a mouthful of embalming fluid or curdled blood and vinegar.

vtmlarp.source: Storytellers Guide, "The Dead and the Damned"
